title: The stack-sorting degree grows faster than 1.80^n: a refutation of the Defant–Propp interval conjecture
exact_endpoint: StackSort.Round6.mathdb_345545 : ¬ Conj (Conj := ∃ L, Tendsto (fun n => deg n ^ (1/n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 L) ∧ L ∈ Ioo 1.68 1.73, deg n = P n / n!, P n the literal fibre-pair count of West's stack-sorting map); limit_ge : every such limit is ≥ 1.73; nonvacuity : ∃ᶠ n, 1.73 < deg n ^ (1/n); subsequence_companion; plus mathdb_345545_max and max_companion for the MathDB maximum-fibre paraphrase (no credit)
scope: Defant and Propp, arXiv:2002.07144 v3/v4 Conjecture 4.4 (Electron. J. Combin. 27(3) (2020) P3.51, Conjecture 23), restated as open by Defant (Adv. Math. 2022): the limit lies in (1.68, 1.73). False: every limit is at least 1.73 (Lean), and the exact values through n = 82 give at least 1.80468 (ordinary exact computation); the numerical value is about 1.95.
formalization_lanes: stacksort-formal-r1, r2a, r2b, r3, r4, r5a, r5b, r6
substantive_reason: It refutes a published conjecture (EJC 2020) that Defant restated as open in Adv. Math. 2022, where the best bound was 1.62924. The refutation needs exact values of P_n never published (brute force stops near n = 14) together with a new root-split inequality; the new exact polynomial-time top-max recursion gives P_n through n = 82, the bound 1.80468 and the estimate of about 1.95, and explains why the authors' sampling estimated the typical rather than the mean growth. Significance is moderate: the reviewer showed that exact P_1..P_13 plus the root-split inequality already suffice for the bare refutation.
novelty_standard: Qualified bounded comparison; not worldwide priority
remaining_literature_limits: Google Scholar, MathSciNet and zbMATH not consulted
